Makhnivka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Makhnivka's name has changed repeatedly: first mentioned in 1430, when the Tyszkiewicz family's progenitor received it from the Grand Duke of Lithuania Svidrigaila, it was renamed Komsomolske in 1935 before the original name was finally restored in 2016. Jews are first mentioned there in 1648, during the Cossack-Polish War, when Khmelnytsky's forces attacked the local fortress and killed a number of Poles and Jews alongside them. The Jewish population reached 2,435 of 5,343 residents by 1897, supporting a synagogue and four prayer houses. A Hasidic dynasty was established in Makhnivka in the early 20th century and continues to flourish in Israel today. By the 1939 outbreak of WWII, the Jewish population of Komsomolske (as the town was then known) had fallen to 843; the Germans captured the town on July 14, 1941, and executed 835 Jews in a nearby forest on September 9. In 2019, this cemetery was fenced by the ESJF.
